name: Universal Recording Corporation
description: Bill Putnam's pioneering Chicago studio -- founded in Evanston in 1946, moved to the 42nd floor of the Chicago Civic Opera Building in 1947, then to 46 E. Walton Street in 1955 as the city's largest independent studio; first artistic use of artificial reverb (the Harmonicats' 'Peg o' My Heart'), first single-artist overdub; clients included Vee-Jay, Mercury, Chess, and One-derful. Putnam received a posthumous Technical Grammy as the 'Father of Modern Recording' in 2000.

name: Uncle Waffles
description: Uncle Waffles, born Lungelihle Zwane on 30 March 2000 in Eswatini (formerly Swaziland) and based in South Africa, is a DJ and producer whom Billboard calls the "Princess of Amapiano." A former presenter on Eswatini TV's Studio1, where she first encountered DJ decks, she learned to DJ during the 2020 lockdowns. Her breakthrough came in October 2021, when a clip of her dancing to Young Stunna's "Adiwele" at Zone 6, Soweto, went viral. Her debut single "Tanzania" (2022) reached No. 1 in South Africa and is certified 7× platinum there; the EPs Red Dragon (2022), Asylum and Solace (2023) followed, Asylum certified gold by RiSA within a week. A BBC Radio 1 residency was announced in September 2022, and in April 2023 she became the first amapiano artist to perform at Coachella.

name: Usher
aliases: Usher Terry Raymond IV; Usher Raymond IV
description: Usher (born Usher Terry Raymond IV on October 14, 1978, in Dallas, Texas, and raised in Chattanooga, Tennessee, and Atlanta, Georgia) is an American singer, dancer, and entertainer who helped define mainstream R&B from the late 1990s onward. Signed to LaFace Records as a teenager, he released his self-titled debut in 1994 and broke through with My Way (1997) and 8701 (2001). His fourth album, Confessions (2004), was certified Diamond in the United States and produced four Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 singles, including the Lil Jon and Ludacris collaboration that dominated 2004. He sustained that run through later No. 1 albums and singles, a Las Vegas residency, and a headlining performance at the Super Bowl LVIII halftime show on February 11, 2024, the same week he released the album Coming Home.

name: Univision Communications
description: Univision Communications is a Spanish-language media conglomerate. In CultureTechLens's media-ownership research, its significance is a four-year hold on The Root, the Black news and culture publication. Univision acquired The Root in May 2015 — from the Slate Group, part of Graham Holdings — as part of a digital expansion targeting communities of color; the price was undisclosed, and The Root, then drawing about five million unique users a month by ComScore's count, retained editorial control while gaining access to Univision's digital production infrastructure. In April 2019 The Root left Univision as part of the Gizmodo Media Group, which Great Hill Partners bought from Univision to form the newly created G/O Media — the next link in the ownership chain CTL traces for the publication.

name: UWG (UniWorld Group)
description: UWG (UniWorld Group) is a New York-based multicultural advertising agency founded in 1969 by Byron Lewis, and one of the oldest African American-owned agencies in the United States. In 2000 Lewis sold a 49 percent stake to the global holding company WPP as a strategic alliance; when he retired in 2012, he sold his remaining stake to Monique Nelson and her family, and the firm rebranded as UWG in 2014. It remains minority-owned and woman-led — Lori-Laine Holdings holds 51 percent and WPP 49 percent — operating as a strategic partner of the WPP network under CEO Monique L. Nelson.

name: United Shoe Machinery Company
description: The United Shoe Machinery Company is the shoe-machinery company that acquired Jan Ernst Matzeliger's lasting-machine patent after his death. Matzeliger, a Surinamese-American inventor working in Lynn, Massachusetts, received U.S. Patent 274,207 for the lasting machine on March 20, 1883; the machine mechanized shoe lasting and transformed shoe manufacturing, producing 150 to 700 pairs of shoes per day against about 50 by a skilled hand laster and cutting shoe prices across the nation roughly in half. In 1889 the Consolidated Lasting Machine Company was formed to manufacture his devices, with Matzeliger retaining substantial ownership; he died of tuberculosis in Lynn on August 24, 1889, aged 36, and the United Shoe Machinery Company acquired his patent thereafter.

name: Usher Board
description: Usher boards are the lay ministry of doorkeepers in Black churches — 'watchmen and watchwomen' who run the sanctuary's infrastructure of order and welcome. Ushers arrive about an hour before service to prepare programs and offering envelopes, greet and seat worshippers (including latecomers), stand watch throughout the service, communicate through as many as 23 silent hand signals, care for worshippers overcome during spirit possession, handle the offerings, and are among the last to leave. Ushers are described in the African American Lectionary's cultural resources as 'the initial source of love and welcome,' trained also through the Nurses Guild auxiliary in CPR and first aid, and honored annually on Usher's Day.

name: Urban Girl Adventures
aliases: Urban Girls: Adventures of Little Ladies in the City
description: Urban Girl Adventures is a children's book series created by Chicago author Asadah Kirkland with her daughter Patience, launched in 2012 with Urban Girls: Adventures of Little Ladies in the City — Travel. The first volume is a 32-page paperback (ISBN 9780983620501) published by Asadah Sense Consulting. Per Kirkland's literary biography, the series combines Patience's photography — taken when she was seven — with her mother's words, to show how children live in urban environments. The series later extended to screen: a webisode, “Urban Girls Travel,” first aired in 2017, mirroring the first book. A companion site, urbangirladventures.com, remains live with its 2014 Asadah Sense Consulting footer.

name: Underground Railroad
description: The Underground Railroad was the clandestine practice — part network, part shared discipline of shelter, guidance, and forwarding — by which enslaved people escaped to freedom, aided by antislavery Americans, Black and white, in the decades before the Civil War. Chicago was one of its northern hubs: routes from Illinois towns along the Mississippi and Ohio rivers ended here, and the city's Black community, led by figures such as tailor John Jones and his wife Mary Jones, sheltered freedom seekers and moved them on toward Canada. Quinn Chapel AME Church, Chicago's oldest Black congregation, holds a documented station tradition and was the city's first site listed in the National Park Service's Network to Freedom registry. After the Fugitive Slave Act of 1850 made even free Black Chicagoans vulnerable to seizure, many fled onward to Canada in the exodus of early 1861.

name: US Studios
description: US Studios was Robert Williams's mid-1970s Chicago party venture, the organizational predecessor of the Warehouse. A New Yorker formed by that city's disco club culture, Williams arrived in Chicago in 1973, found little comparable nightlife, and began hosting DJ-led dance parties at a series of former industrial venues in the West Loop and South Loop, as documented in the City of Chicago landmark report. The parties moved through several addresses before settling at 206 S. Jefferson in 1977 as the Warehouse proper. US Studios matters to the graph because it shows the Warehouse was an iterated experiment in rooms before it was a famous one.
